public_rationale: On 13 July 2025, Marcus wrote that symbol grounding had not been systematically solved. A survey submitted on 6 January 2025 lists symbol grounding among the foundational problems LLMs must address to reach human-level general intelligence (e1). A paper posted on 9 June 2025 says the field had no shared scoring criteria, which made it hard to say when a solution had been achieved (e2). The same paper reports that Steels argued the problem had been 'solved' to some extent, while also setting out a new challenge (e3). That account is qualified. It does not describe an accepted general solution. No item in the packet reports a broadly accepted, general, reproducible solution before the post. This meets the contract's support condition.
limitations: The claim says something does not exist. The finding rests on how two 2025 preprints describe the field, not on a formal consensus statement.
Both sources are preprints, not peer-reviewed papers.
Steels's partial-solution view is reported secondhand through the June 2025 paper. The packet does not show how widely that view is held.
Work published after 13 July 2025 falls outside the target period and was not assessed.

statement.document_title: How o3 and Grok 4 Accidentally Vindicated Neurosymbolic AI

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post (July 2025), the research field had no accepted, general solution to the symbol grounding problem. Researchers still treated it as an open problem.
No period is named, so the target period is the first half of 2025 up to the post date. That is the most recent literature that could describe the state of the field when he wrote.
criteria.support_condition: Research from 2025 before the post treats symbol grounding as an unsolved or open foundational problem, or says there is no agreed standard for calling it solved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Research before the post reports a broadly accepted, general, reproducible solution to symbol grounding for AI systems.

evidence.excerpt: A number of foundational problems -- embodiment, symbol grounding, causality and memory -- are required to be addressed for LLMs to attain human-level general intelligence.
evidence.explanation: This 2025 survey treats symbol grounding as a foundational problem LLMs still need to address. That fits 'not systematically solved'.

evidence.excerpt: Moreover, the absence of shared scoring criteria has made it difficult to determine when and how a solution to either problem might be said to have been achieved.
evidence.explanation: A June 2025 paper says the field had no shared criteria for even calling symbol grounding solved. That supports the claim that no systematic solution was accepted.

evidence.excerpt: Steels argued that the symbol grounding problem itself has been “solved” to some extent, but presented a new challenge of constructing autonomous meaning networks [13].
evidence.explanation: A minority view holds that grounding is partly solved. Even this view is qualified ('to some extent') and names a remaining challenge, so it does not show a systematic solution.
